root_cause.text: A race condition in IPv6 anycast join where a new anycast address (aca) is added to the per-device list under idev->lock but inserted into the global hash (inet6_acaddr_lst) after the lock is released, allowing a concurrent teardown to remove it from the per-device list, drop its reference, and free it before the hash insertion completes, leaving a dangling pointer in the hash for RCU readers.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and commit message explicitly describe the window: "It is published to idev->ac_list under idev->lock, but ipv6_add_acaddr_hash() runs after write_unlock_bh(). A concurrent teardown ... can slip into that window" and the patch moves ipv6_add_acaddr_hash() inside the idev->lock section. The acaddr_hash_lock is also switched to spin_lock_bh() to avoid lock inversion.
